correctness.rationale: The three disk zeros 1/2 and 1/2±i sqrt(3)/6 multiply to the stated rational function. With x=tan(theta/2)^2, the exact boundary phase identity is psi′=7-2688x^3/[(1+9x)(1+2x+49x^2)], with positive denominator, unique maximum slope 7 and order-five zero of psi″ at theta=0; the only other zero, at pi, is simple with phase slope 19/21. Uniform dyadic second-derivative van der Corput estimates give O(n^-1/7) uniformly in integer k; exact order-seven stationary phase at k=7n gives Gamma(1/7)cos(pi/14)/(7*pi*6^(1/7)). At degree m every centered phase-derivative difference is a nonzero rational function of Cayley coordinate of numerator degree <=2m unless the phase derivative is constant, so the highest possible local order is 2m and sup coefficients O(n^(-1/(2m+1))). In particular degrees 1 and 2 decay faster; monomials have supremum one. Independently factored the rational polynomial, recomputed exact slope and endpoint, and numerically checked gamma constant ~0.224736168618. Finite quadrature cannot alone establish a limit.
